A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 21-page versions of the same DisCO paper. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main text, figures, tables, equations, Algorithm 1, and Appendices A–B without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original mathematical-reasoning fine-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons, training dynamics, and ablations in Section 6 and Appendix A, including Tables 2–5.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix A, including the benchmark comparisons, training dynamics, and ablation studies.

M1.justification: The DisCO and DisCO-b objectives, scoring functions, hard-negative weighting, KL constraint, optimization procedure, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The conclusion's proposed non-binary-reward extension is future work, not an implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DeepScaleR-Preview and DAPO-Math-17K and evaluate on AIME 2024/2025, MATH 500, AMC 2023, Minerva, and Olympiad Bench. The new suggestion to explore other reasoning tasks introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same comparator memberships, including GRPO, GRPO-ER, Dr. GRPO, DAPO, TRPA, and the same reference models. No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the same models, response-length settings, pass@1 metric, training batches, and budgets. Evaluation every 200 steps and reporting each method's best performance are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The difficulty-reweighting analysis, training dynamics, DisCO-versus-DisCO-b comparisons, clipping tests, KL comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity, and component ablations are unchanged. The clipping paragraph receives wording edits without changing its experiment or findings.

E5.justification: Both versions specify pass@1 averaging over 16 generated responses per question. Run and seed information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical estimation procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are retained. For example, DisCO (log-L)'s average pass@1 remains 0.533 in Table 2 and 0.541 in Table 5. Table 4's 0.579 entry changes only in font weight.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, mathematical objectives, derivations, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. Removing a stray comma from an expectation in Section 4 is a typographical correction without mathematical consequences.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about eliminating difficulty bias, stabilizing training, and improving mathematical reasoning. The binary-reward scope was already explicit in v3; the added future-work discussion does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds a concrete proposal to use discriminative ranking objectives for non-binary rewards, alongside future applications to larger models and other reasoning tasks. These extension directions are new, while the binary-reward assumption and existing result interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 6's hyperparameters and training details, Algorithm 1, Appendix A's hardware and timing disclosures, and the code-access footnote are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged. The conclusion reuses the existing learning-to-rank reference [9] for a future extension, without adding a cited work or revising the current method's novelty and positioning against prior methods.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized author-line, punctuation, and grammar edits, lightly rewrites the clipping paragraph, and adds two concluding sentences. The section organization and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adjusts author spacing, reduces the gap before Figure 4, and reflows page 10. Table 4 removes bold emphasis from the 0.579 average while retaining bold 0.584. Plot content, table structure, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves the paper through a specific discussion of extending beyond binary rewards, small language corrections, and corrected emphasis in Table 4. These improve the conclusion and presentation, while the methods, empirical evidence, theory, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
